We roll on MONDAY! (Last full cycle before the summer hols…😱🤯) YOU IN?!
🎙What is TOMM and How Can it Help You? All the info you need about TOMM is over on the link in my bio ❤️❤️❤️❤️ Gem x

This is THE most asked question, so let's get it answered. 👇👇👇👇
⁠
❤️Firstly if you're new then welcome, you're going to LOVE it here! I will hold your hand and walk you back to calm. ⁠
⁠
🏡If your house is in need of a housework reset then check out the Messy House Bootcamp or the Clutter Buster (both of which are free to download on the blog - the link is in my bio).⁠
⁠
🙌Then you can jump into the 30-minute-a-day method (the method is also free to download via the link in my bio). Don't worry if the rest of TeamTOMM is not on week 1 - just jump in wherever we are, you don't have to wait until the start of a new cycle. ⁠
⁠
💻 Join the free Facebook group (search The Organised Mum Community). You'll find loads of friendly faces (140k(ish) at the last count) all there to support and lift you up(there is no such thing as a silly question).⁠
⁠
📱If you have tried the free printouts and want to make TOMM more specific to you and your lifestyle then there is the TeamTOMM app (android and apple). Which will help you to change the days around and make up your own cleaning lists. ⁠
⁠
There’s loads more I can tell you about ... the three books, the podcast, and the guided clean-a-longs on Patreon but I don't want to overwhelm you if you're new. Start with the above and if you want to know more then please check out the link in my bio. ⁠
⁠
If you have any questions the support team are an email away on support@theorganisedmum.blog ⁠
⁠
Great to have you here ❤️ Gem ❤️

Hey there if you’re new 👋👋 The Organised Mum Method (TOMM) is a realistic way to keep on top of your home. I created it 16 years ago when I was struggling to keep on top of the housework as a new mum. If you want to have a home that looks great, have weekends that are free of cleaning AND still have time in the week to get on with the stuff that you actually enjoy … then you are in the right place.
.
​​So How Does it Work?.
.
​​There are 3 levels of jobs and if you want a handy tick-list with suggested jobs for each room then you can download all the printables for free! Just hit the link at the top of this page. 
.
Before you get started though: I want you to look at the lists of jobs as suggestions. A bit like a pick and mix of things that you can do. If you want to truly customise TOMM then you can download the TeamTOMM app and make TOMM fit you and your home to a T!
.
So glad you’ve found the page 😍
All next week on the #TeamTOMM podcast it is #hallowclean 👻 so get ready for some spooky fun and expect the unexpected!

latestPosts.caption: It’s almost time for #organisedchristmas 😍😍 We start Monday 7th Sept

September has a habit of making us think we need to become a new, more organised version of ourselves 😇

But before you start creating systems for packed lunches, laundry, paperwork, mornings, evenings and every other moving part of family life, give it a minute.

Let normal life start happening again first. Then watch where it gets stuck.

What are you constantly reminding people about? What can nobody ever find? What piles up in the same place? Which bit of the day regularly descends into chaos? And what decision are you suck to the back teeth of making?

That’s where I’d put your effort. Because being organised isn’t about having a system for everything. It’s about having a few good systems in the places that genuinely make life easier. Don’t spend this week trying to optimise the entire household.

**Find the friction. Then fix the friction.**

And if you’ve already spotted yours, tell me in the comments. Give me your household problem and I’ll see if I can fix it.
Organised Christmas starts Sept 7th🎄If you’ve got any questions pop them below ❤️❤️
Back that school back to routine …. 💋🎉😍#cleaningroutine #cleaningmotivation #theorganisedmum #mentalload

Tiredness can make a messy house feel personal. Nothing necessarily has become worse but your tolerance is on the floor and you have no spare capacity for what you can see needs doing. 

When these days come along pick the things that restore function. Don’t try to drag an impressive reset out of an exhausted person, just try and make tomorrow a little easier ❤️🩷

And remember just do your best with the time and you have xxx
Non performative home and life organisation you say? Hold my tea …
Does your mind still race when you’re sitting down? Do you jump up from the sofa when someone walks in because you feel guilty for being ‘caught’ resting? 👀😩 You don’t need to earn your rest ❤️
There’s a big stretch of domestic space between a show home and complete chaos. Decide where you want your to home to sit in that space. This js your good enough.

Ready to get out of your constantly-looking-for-a-new-cleaning-routine era? Because I promise you, the answer probably isn’t another routine.

It’s very easy to get stuck in the cycle of finding a new system, feeling wildly motivated for three days, missing a day and then deciding the whole thing doesn’t work.

But a good routine shouldn’t require perfect conditions to keep it going. It needs to work when you’re busy. When the kids are home and when work is ridiculously hectic. 

The aim isn’t to find a routine you can follow perfectly. It’s to find one you can come back to easily. And one that is realistic enough that you’re not forever feeling behind. That’s the bit we sometimes miss.

You don’t need another fresh start. You need something boringly reliable that gives you more time to get on with your actual life.

And yes, that is pretty much why I created TOM.

it’s boring and overwhelming. This morning I was cleaning the shower. And I became acutely aware of the monotony of it. I’ve cleaned that shower hundreds of times before. I’ll no doubt clean it hundreds of times again. There will never be a point at which someone taps me on the shoulder and says, “Congratulations Gemma. You’ve completed showers!”

And this is perhaps the most uncomfortable bit about running a home. It is both boring and overwhelming at exactly the same time. The overwhelm gets plenty of airtime. But we rarely acknowledge the boredom. 

The work of maintaining a home is made up of tasks that are endlessly repetitive. Laundry. Beds. Dishes. Floors. Bathrooms. Bins. Meals. And they regenerate at an astonishing rate. There is no lasting sense of completion because tomorrow usually undoes most of today’s effort.

Humans aren’t particularly well designed for this either. We’re motivated by progress and enjoy novelty. We like beginnings, middles and endings. Housework offers none of that. Instead, it rewards you with having to do it again.

And the exhaustion isn’t coming from the physical act of wiping a sink. It’s the fact that it is not one job. It’s fifty jobs, many of them invisible. And maybe that is why we search so desperately for hacks.

The magical storage solution. The miracle cleaning product. Trying to solve a problem that isn’t really about cleaning at all. We’re trying to make repetitive work feel finite.

I didn’t have a lightbulb moment in the shower but I do know that acceptance can be surprisingly freeing. Not resignation, just acceptance.

Accepting that homes are living things. They get messy because people live in them. Laundry is evidence of people having clothes to wear and dirty dishes are the aftermath of meals eaten. A shower that needs cleaning is simply proof that people are (thankfully) washing.

The work isn’t failing because it comes back because that’s exactly what it’s supposed to do. Tomorrow, the shower will need another quick wipe. Like the final boss at the end of the video game that just keeps on regenerating …

Staying ahead of the house is NOT about spotless rooms. It’s about doing the small things before they become big things. A made bed, dishes done, a quick wash on. Tiny jobs that stop the build-up. The mess will come back (of course it will) but you’re never quite starting from scratch ❤️🩷
